sources.name: OGC GeoTIFF Standard 1.1
sources.role: georeferenced TIFF encoding, raster-to-model metadata and EPSG-aligned CRS contract
verified_facts: GeoTIFF 1.1 specifies requirements and encoding rules for exchanging georeferenced or geocoded imagery in TIFF.
The standard aligns GeoTIFF metadata with the EPSG Geodetic Parameter Dataset.
GeoTIFF is an encoding used broadly for geographic image data exchange.
semantic_limits: GeoTIFF conformance does not establish source authority, complete download, native survey resolution or vertical accuracy.
CRS and raster-to-model metadata must be read back from the exact full-resolution object.
A valid TIFF or GeoTIFF file must not create a parcel-height row without polygon, datum, unit, pixel-validity and digest receipts.

sources.name: OGC Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF Standard 1.0
sources.role: tiled TIFF, reduced-resolution subfile and HTTP range retrieval contract
verified_facts: Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF uses TIFF tiles, reduced-resolution subfiles, GeoTIFF georeferencing and HTTP range requests.
COG-aware clients can retrieve selected byte ranges instead of downloading an entire object.
The standard is designed for efficient Web visualization and geospatial processing.
semantic_limits: A successful range request or overview decode is not proof that the full-resolution source object was retrieved.
Reduced-resolution subfiles must not be sampled as native one-metre elevation evidence.
Partial byte coverage must not be treated as complete-object integrity or parcel measurement proof.

sources.name: OGC Web Coverage Service (WCS) Standard
sources.role: multidimensional coverage retrieval, mandatory core and extension-bound response contract
verified_facts: WCS provides Internet access to multidimensional geospatial coverages.
WCS coverages can represent regular or irregular grids, point clouds and general meshes.
Core requirements are mandatory, while extensions specify additional capabilities such as response encodings.
semantic_limits: WCS success does not independently prove coverage freshness, complete payload, vertical datum or terrain accuracy.
Coverage identifier, subset axes, encoding, CRS, range component and response digest must remain bound.
Service availability and HTTP success must not create a business measurement.

sources.name: OGC CoverageJSON Community Standard 1.0
sources.role: Web-oriented JSON coverage, domain/range and partitioned-document contract
verified_facts: CoverageJSON is a JSON format for publishing spatiotemporal coverage data to Web clients.
It can encode gridded and non-gridded coverages with continuous or categorical values.
Large datasets can be partitioned among multiple documents, while the format is not intended to replace efficient binary bulk formats.
semantic_limits: CoverageJSON readability or schema validity does not establish numeric source accuracy.
Partitioned documents or null values require explicit completeness and missing-value handling.
A JSON value must not become parcel-height evidence without exact source, geometry, CRS, datum, unit, method and execution receipts.

sources.name: OGC Geography Markup Language (GML) Standard
sources.role: XML geographic feature, geometry, property and application-schema exchange contract
verified_facts: GML is an XML grammar for expressing geographic features and their spatial and non-spatial properties.
GML supports points, lines and polygons and allows community-specific application schemas.
GML is used as an interchange format by geospatial services including WFS.
semantic_limits: XML or schema validity does not prove authoritative parcel identity or legal boundary status.
Geometry source, CRS, axis order, precision and object digest must remain explicit.
Equivalent parsed geometry must not replace exact downloaded bytes and containment receipts.

sources.name: OGC Web Feature Service (WFS) Standard
sources.role: feature discovery, query, property access, locking and transaction contract
verified_facts: WFS provides fine-grained access to geographic features and their properties.
The standard defines discovery and query operations and also supports locking and transactions.
OGC identifies OGC API Features as the newer Web API approach for comparable feature-access capabilities.
semantic_limits: A feature query result is a service representation and not proof of complete or authoritative cadastral source bytes.
Filtering and returned geometry do not by themselves establish exact HMLR point-in-polygon binding.
Transaction or query success must not be interpreted as terrain measurement accuracy.

sources.name: OGC API - Features Standard
sources.role: collection and feature retrieval, WGS84 core and additional-CRS contract
verified_facts: OGC API Features defines modular Web API building blocks for interacting with geospatial features.
Part 1 Core fetches features in WGS 84 longitude-latitude order, while Part 2 supports other coordinate reference systems.
The API provides direct object-level access rather than requiring transfer of an entire dataset.
semantic_limits: Object-level retrieval does not prove that the complete authoritative collection was examined.
WGS84 response coordinates must not replace native EPSG:27700 parcel containment where native geometry is available.
API conformance, filtering and HTTP success do not establish elevation semantics or vertical accuracy.

sources.name: OGC API - Common - Part 1: Core
sources.role: reusable Web API landing, conformance and API-definition building-block contract
verified_facts: OGC API Common defines reusable building blocks applicable across OGC Web API standards.
It standardizes fundamental resources and requirements used to construct coherent modular APIs.
The standard separates reusable API capabilities from domain-specific resource semantics.
semantic_limits: A conformance declaration describes implemented API modules, not accuracy or completeness of a response.
Landing pages and API definitions are service metadata rather than terrain source objects.
Shared API behavior must not substitute for source bytes, exact geometry, datum and measurement receipts.

sources.name: OGC Observations, Measurements, and Samples (OMS)
sources.role: observation act, feature-of-interest, sample, result and procedure context contract
verified_facts: OMS defines a conceptual schema for observations, involved features and sampling features.
It supports exchange of observation acts and results across scientific and technical communities.
The model distinguishes the ultimate feature of interest from spatial, material or statistical samples.
semantic_limits: A numeric result without procedure, observed property, feature-of-interest, sample and time bindings is not measurement evidence.
Observation-model conformance does not establish source authority or parcel-specific vertical accuracy.
Sample identity must not be silently equated with exact cadastral polygon identity.

sources.name: OGC Web Coverage Processing Service (WCPS) 1.1
sources.role: coverage extraction, processing, aggregation and analysis-language contract
verified_facts: WCPS defines a protocol-independent language for extracting, processing and analysing multidimensional coverages.
It is designed for coverages representing sensor, image or statistical data.
Processing expressions can derive results from addressed coverage data.
semantic_limits: A successfully evaluated processing expression does not prove source completeness, accuracy or authority.
Aggregates must exclude nodata values and remain bound to the exact input coverage and parameters.
Derived values must not become parcel-height evidence without reproducible source and execution receipts.

sources.name: OGC Web Service Common 2.0
sources.role: common OGC Web-service request, response, exception and metadata structure contract
verified_facts: OWS Common defines parameters and data structures shared by multiple OGC Web Service standards.
Its purpose is to avoid repeating common request and response material across service specifications.
Service-specific standards normatively reference applicable common components.
semantic_limits: A common request or exception structure is transport metadata rather than source-quality evidence.
Service metadata and successful parsing do not validate terrain values or parcel geometry.
Error-free protocol handling must not be promoted to measurement success.

sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.name: FIPS 180-4 Secure Hash Standard
sources.role: SHA message-digest computation and post-digest change-detection contract
verified_facts: FIPS 180-4 specifies secure hash algorithms used to generate message digests.
Message digests can be used to detect whether messages changed after digest generation.
SHA-256 is part of the Secure Hash Standard family defined by the publication.
semantic_limits: A matching digest establishes byte identity only relative to the hashed object and algorithm.
Hash equality does not establish publisher authority, semantic correctness, completeness before hashing or measurement accuracy.
A digest must remain bound to the exact source object, acquisition time and processing receipt.
